prompt.brief: Design a real-time sentiment platform that ingests social, review, and support streams, performs multilingual aspect-level analysis, and detects meaningful trend shifts with provenance.
successSignals: Define source connectors, deduplication, language detection, sentiment/emotion/aspect outputs, confidence, provenance, and deletion semantics.
Aggregate results by brand, topic, aspect, geography, and time window while handling bot noise, late events, changing taxonomies, and sampling bias.
Separate streaming ingestion and model inference from dashboard queries; support model versioning, replay, and at-least-once processing.
Explain shift alerts, privacy, human review, model fallback, failure recovery, observability, and a degraded mode.

functional: Ingest authorized posts, reviews, and feedback, normalize and deduplicate them, then classify sentiment, emotion, language, and aspects with confidence.
Expose near-real-time aggregates, representative evidence, trend charts, and alerts by tenant, brand, topic, aspect, locale, and time window.
Support source deletion requests, reprocessing with a new model, analyst feedback, alert acknowledgment, and replay after consumer failure.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 end-to-end processing under 2 seconds for sampled events and alert within five minutes of a sustained shift.
Scale to millions of messages per hour across many brands and languages without unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Millions of messages/hour across many languages
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Real-time sentiment platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Real-time sentiment platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Real-time sentiment platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Real-time sentiment platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Real-time sentiment platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Real-time sentiment platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Real-time sentiment platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Real-time sentiment platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Real-time sentiment platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
